title: Task Dependency Order
statement: Read n (number of tasks, numbered 0 to n-1) and m (number of dependency edges), then m lines each with two integers 'a b' meaning task a must run before task b. Print one valid execution order covering all n tasks: at each step, among the tasks whose prerequisites are all satisfied, always pick the smallest task number next. If the dependencies contain a cycle so not all tasks can be ordered, print 'CYCLE' instead.
starter_code:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
indegree = [0] * n
for _ in range(m):
    a, b = map(int, input().split())
    adj[a].append(b)
    indegree[b] += 1

# TODO: run Kahn's algorithm for topological sort. Among tasks with

# can't place all n tasks, print "CYCLE"; otherwise print the order as
# space-separated task numbers.
hints: Use heapq as a min-heap seeded with every task that starts at indegree 0
Each time you pop a task, decrement the indegree of its neighbors and push any that drop to 0
If the final order has fewer than n tasks, a cycle blocked some of them
